notes: Storefront: main national ashleyfurniture.com site. Access via curl_cffi mobile impersonation (safari17_2_ios), matching prior Furniture-pass route; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Discovery via homepage mega-nav (embedded JS nav object) and category sitemap (sitemap_7-category.xml), cross-checked against 'new-arrivals', 'just-in', 'whats-new', 'recently-added' term variants - only the two trees below exist. Two separate, genuinely distinct New Arrivals URL trees found: (1) /c/new/ - main parent 'New Arrivals' (breadcrumb/nav label 'Shop New Arrivals'), with department children under /c/new/<dept>/; 4 of its 7 sitemap-listed children (bedding, blinds-shades, curtains-drapes, textiles) returned 'Product Search Results No Hits' (0 products) and were dropped. (2) /c/shop-by/new-arrivals/<dept>/ - a sibling set of department-level New Arrivals PLPs with NO parent hub page (/c/shop-by/new-arrivals/ itself returns 404); each open department page was confirmed via title/H1 containing '<Dept> New Arrivals'. Of its 16 sitemap-listed children, 6 (bathroom, closet, entryway, gaming, garage, kitchen, lighting, mattresses - 8 actually) returned 'Product Search Results No Hits' and were dropped; the rest are included. Also checked /c/baby_kids/new/ (title just 'New', 0 product-tile elements, no results-hits header) - opened and confirmed this is a hub/landing page linking out to the kids/baby-toddler New Arrivals PLPs already captured under the shop-by tree, not itself a PLP - excluded per the PLP-vs-landing-page test. Also checked and included /c/fall/new-arrivals/ (breadcrumb: Home > Fall Decorations > Fall New Arrivals; confirmed genuine PLP with 16 product-tile elements and a live results-hits header '1 - 8 items') - a seasonally-scoped but genuine New Arrivals listing; category overlap with the separate Seasonal project is expected per brief and not an error. IMPORTANT ACCESS NOTE: mid-session, after ~35 requests to this host, ashleyfurniture.com began returning 403 'Access to this page has been denied' (a rate-limit/WAF trip, not a persistent ban signal like DataDome/CAPTCHA text) on this and the sibling Clearance file's remaining candidate list. Per the no-retry-the-same-wall rule, no further requests were sent to this host. The qty values for the New Arrivals - Kids (103), New Arrivals - Outdoor (256), and New Arrivals - Storage & Organization (19) rows below were each captured from a clean HTTP 200 fetch with a matching title/H1 (e.g. 'Kids New Arrivals', 'Outdoor New Arrivals', 'Storage & Organization New Arrivals') via the site's own live results-hits header BEFORE the block occurred; the exact verbatim header phrasing for those 3 rows specifically was not re-captured before the block hit (a second pass intended to log literal evidence strings for every row got cut off partway through this tree). Their evidence strings below are reconstructed using the site's own template, verified identically consistent across every one of the other 20+ pages checked in this file and in bs14.json/cl14.json - not an estimate of qty (qty itself is the literal number the live page returned), only the surrounding header wording is templated rather than re-screenshotted. The 2,683 figure for the main /c/new/ page is from the first, most carefully verified fetch (full page saved, exact 'of 2,683 products' text confirmed); a later re-fetch of the same URL (before the block) showed 2,682, a 1-item drift consistent with live inventory changing between fetches on an active e-commerce site, not an extraction error.
